Restricting and pasting cone diagrams

The pullback pasting lemma uses compatibility of chosen factorizations with restriction and pasting. These calculations must retain the matching identification of each cone. All categories below are absolute, with the Chapter 1 coherence and pullback structure.

For \(f\colon C\to E\) and \(g\colon D\to E\), a cone on \(T\) is \(s=(p,q,\tau )\) with \(\tau \colon fp=gq\). A comparison to \(s'=(p',q',\tau ')\) consists of \(L\colon p=p'\), \(R\colon q=q'\), and \[ \tau '\cdot (f\star L)=(g\star R)\cdot \tau . \] The symbol \(\star \) denotes whiskering; vertical composition applies the rightmost factor first. Write \(\alpha _{r,p,f}\colon (fp)r=f(pr)\). These descriptions concern data of cones and comparisons, without requiring a category of all cones.

Supplementary Lemma 1. Restriction by \(r\colon S\to T\) sends \(s\) to the cone \(r^*s\) with legs \(pr,qr\) and matching \[ \alpha _{r,q,g}\cdot (\tau \star r)\cdot \alpha _{r,p,f}^{-1}. \] It takes cone comparisons to cone comparisons. There is a comparison \(\mathrm {id}^*s\to s\) with the right unitors as leg comparisons. For \(u\colon U\to T\) and \(r\colon S\to U\), there is also a comparison \(r^*(u^*s)\to (u\circ r)^*s\) with the associators as leg comparisons.

Proof idea

Prewhisker the two leg comparisons and their matching equation. The mixed whiskering law and associator compatibility put the resulting equation into the displayed form. For identity restriction, use compatibility of the right unitor with a composite. For successive restriction, the pentagon compares the associators on the two routes. Reassociate vertical composites to obtain the required matching equation. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Let \(f\colon A\to B\), \(g\colon B\to Z\), \(h\colon X\to Z\), and let \(t=(u,v,\nu )\) be a cone over \((g,h)\) on \(Q\). A cone \(s=(p,q,\rho )\) over \((f,u)\) on \(T\) determines a cone \(\operatorname {Flat}_t(s)\) over \((gf,h)\) with legs \(p,vq\) and matching \[ \operatorname {match}(q^*t)\cdot (g\star \rho )\cdot \alpha _{p,f,g}. \] Flattening takes cone comparisons to cone comparisons. Moreover, \(r^*\operatorname {Flat}_t(s)\) compares with \(\operatorname {Flat}_t(r^*s)\) by the identity on the left leg and \(\alpha _{r,q,v}\) on the right leg.

Proof idea

Postwhisker the matching equation for a comparison of the inner cones by \(g\), and paste it with the equation for the corresponding restrictions of \(t\). The resulting equation is precisely compatibility of the flattened comparisons.

For restriction, the intermediate cone obtained from \(t\) can be restricted either successively by \(q,r\), or by \(qr\). Apply Supplementary Lemma 1 to compare these cones, then flatten. The leg comparisons normalize to the identity and the displayed associator. Their matching equation is retained during this normalization. □

Supplementary Lemma 3. Suppose \(t\) is a pullback cone. Put \(N=A\times _B Q\) and \(O=A\times _Z X\). Flattening the defining cone of \(N\) induces an equivalence \(F\colon N\to O\). If \(\ell _s\colon T\to N\) and \(\ell _{\operatorname {Flat}_t(s)}\colon T\to O\) are the chosen factorization functors, then \[ \ell _{\operatorname {Flat}_t(s)}=F\circ \ell _s. \] Consequently, \(s\) is a pullback cone if and only if \(\operatorname {Flat}_t(s)\) is a pullback cone.

Proof idea

The defining cone of \(O\) gives a cone over \((g,h)\). Factor it through \(t\) to obtain \(O\to Q\), then lift the resulting cone over \((f,u)\) to obtain \(O\to N\). The two inverse comparisons follow from the pullback universal properties, using full cone comparisons.

For the displayed factorization, flatten the computation comparison for \(\ell _s\) and apply Supplementary Lemma 2 to its restriction. This compares the cone induced by \(F\ell _s\) with the flattened input cone. Reflect through the pullback property of \(O\). A cone is a pullback exactly when its factorization into the chosen pullback is an equivalence; cancellation with \(F\) proves the final assertion. □
